newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares hold their own in jittery trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares hold their own in jittery trade.

text.p: German IBIS DAX index was in positive territory on Wednesday evening, but the prospect of further significant gains was ruled out in the near term by a market rendered jittery after a long period of record highs.

"It's not particularly hectic out there at the moment, but then these are nervous times. We've got a meeting of the Federal Reserve next week and the British elections coming up to make everyone jittery," a trader said.
The 30-share IBIS DAX index stood at 3,309.05 points, up 19.45 points or 0.59 percent in afternoon trade, while DTB DAX futures were up 18.5 points at 3,314.
"The triple-witching later this week also makes the market very superficial and any gains tend to be based on movements in derivatives," the trader said.

Traders said that weaker performances on Wall Street were also dampening sentiment, but said the current slow-down or correction was "not unhealthy". "People will pick up stocks on the way down," a trader said.
Among shares in the news was the engineering group Preussag AG, up 15.70 marks at 457.50 marks, as merger mania in the steel/engineering group lifted the share 3.44 percent to 457 marks.
Focus has centred on the steel industry since Fried. Krupp AG's launched a 13.6 billion mark takeover for Thyssen AG.

Since then Krupp has proposed cooperation talks with Thyssen. The news also boosted Mannesmann AG, which was up 3.37 percent at 644 marks. A slightly weaker dollar at 1.68 marks also impacted on sentiment.
Shares in German drugs group Shering rose initially after it revised its sales and profits forecasts for 1997, but fell amid afternoon profit taking by 45 pfennigs too 156.65 marks.
